subject.name: Mathematics
subject.description: Cambridge International AS & A Level Mathematics. AS Level students take Paper 1 and one of Papers 2, 4 or 5. A Level students take Papers 1 and 3 with either Papers 4 and 5 or Papers 5 and 6. Choose your combination and you will only see its topics and past papers. The questions are original practice questions written in the style of Cambridge papers, not reproduced past paper material.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express 2x² − 12x + 7 in the form a(x + b)² + c. Give your answer in that form.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who first took out the factor of 2 from the x terms were usually successful. A common error was c = −2, from failing to multiply 9 by 2.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the set of values of k for which the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 has no real roots. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the discriminant: k² − 36
M1 for setting k² − 36 < 0 and finding critical values ±6

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the critical values but then gave the incorrect region k < −6, k > 6, or used ≤.

questions.stem: The functions f and g are defined by f(x) = 3x − 2 for x ∈ ℝ and g(x) = 1/(x + 1) for x > −1.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of fg({a}).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found gf({a}) instead. fg(x) means apply g first.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for a correct first step, e.g. x = 3y − 2

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

questions.stem: A circle has equation x² + y² − 6x + 4y − 12 = 0.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the radius of the circle.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates completed the square correctly. Sign errors in the centre were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at the point (6, 2). Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for tangent gradient = −3/4 and use of (6, 2)

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should remember the tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

questions.stem: A sector OAB of a circle has centre O, radius 8 cm and angle AOB = 1.2 radians.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of the sector, in cm².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the area of the segment bounded by the arc AB and the chord AB, in cm², correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for triangle area ½ × 8² × sin 1.2
M1 for sector area − triangle area

parts.examinerComment: A significant number of candidates had their calculators in degree mode, giving sin 1.2° and an incorrect answer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve 2sin²θ − sin θ − 1 = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for factorising: (2 sin θ + 1)(sin θ − 1) = 0
A1 for sin θ = 1 giving θ = 90°
A1 for sin θ = −1/2 giving θ = 210°
A1 for θ = 330° and no extra solutions in range

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates factorised correctly. Many lost the final mark by missing 330° or including extra solutions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of tan(π/3) − 2cos(π/6).
parts.examinerComment: Exact values should be recalled rather than found by calculator.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coefficient of x³ in the expansion of ({a} − x)⁶.
parts.examinerComment: The negative sign was frequently lost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A geometric progression has first term {a} and common ratio {r}. Find the sum to infinity.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

questions.stem: A curve has equation y = x³ − 6x² + 9x + 2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 4.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the stationary points and determine their nature. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using d²y/dx² = 6x − 12 or another valid method

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must give a reason for the nature of each point; stating 'maximum' without justification did not earn the final mark.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Evaluate the integral of ({c}x² − {d}x) with respect to x, from x = 1 to x = {b}.
parts.examinerComment: Arithmetic errors when substituting the lower limit were common.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The region bounded by y = √x, the x-axis and the line x = {k} is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the exact volume of the solid formed, as a multiple of π. Enter the multiple only (e.g. for 5π enter 5).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates integrated √x rather than (√x)². The volume formula requires y².

parts.prompt: Find the set of values of x for which 2x² − 5x − 3 > 0.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates found the critical values but then gave the region between them. A sketch of the parabola avoids this.

parts.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x) = (x − 2)² + 1 for x ≥ 2. Find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for swapping x and y or making x the subject
M1 for (x − 2)² = y − 1 and square rooting

parts.examinerComment: Answers with ± were not accepted: the domain x ≥ 2 means only the positive root applies.

parts.prompt: Find the equation of the line through (1, 4) that is perpendicular to the line 2x + 3y = 7. Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.

markingPoints.text: B1 for gradient of given line = −2/3
M1 for perpendicular gradient 3/2 and use of (1, 4)

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used the gradient 2/3, forgetting the negative reciprocal.

parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius {r} cm and arc length {s} cm. Find the area of the sector, in cm².

markingPoints.text: M1 for angle = {s}/{r} = {=s/r} rad, or area = ½ × r × arc length

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who first found the angle in radians usually succeeded.

parts.prompt: Prove the identity (1 − cos²θ) / (sin θ cos θ) ≡ tan θ.

markingPoints.text: A1 for simplifying sin²θ / (sin θ cos θ) = sin θ / cos θ = tan θ, with no errors

parts.examinerComment: Proofs should start from one side and work clearly to the other. Working on both sides at once is not a valid proof.

parts.prompt: An arithmetic progression has first term {a} and common difference {d}. Find the sum of the first {n} terms.
parts.examinerComment: Using (n − 1)d with n = {n} was essential; some used {n}d.

parts.prompt: A curve has equation y = ({a}x − 1)⁵. Find the gradient of the curve at the point where x = 1.
parts.examinerComment: The factor of {a} from the chain rule was frequently omitted, giving {=5*(a-1)^4}.

parts.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve y = {k}x − x² and the x-axis.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates needed to find where the curve meets the x-axis before integrating.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation |2x − 3| = 5.

markingPoints.text: M1 for 2x − 3 = 5 or 2x − 3 = −5 (or squaring both sides)

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found x = 4. The negative case was often forgotten.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the remainder when x³ − 4x² + x + 6 is divided by (x − {a}).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered using the remainder theorem.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Given that (x + 1) is a factor of x³ + ax² − x − 2, find the value of a.

markingPoints.text: M1 for substituting x = −1 and setting equal to 0

parts.examinerComment: Sign errors when substituting −1 were the main source of lost marks.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation {b}ˣ = {n}, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for x ln {b} = ln {n} or equivalent

parts.examinerComment: Answers to fewer significant figures than asked lost the accuracy mark.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation ln(x + {a}) − ln x = ln {k}.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates wrote ln(x + {a}) − ln x = ln {a}, a misuse of the laws of logarithms.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The variables x and y satisfy y = Ae^(kx). The graph of ln y against x is a straight line with gradient {g} and intercept {c} on the ln y axis. Find A, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should state ln y = ln A + kx before comparing with the straight-line form.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Express 3 sin θ + 4 cos θ in the form R sin(θ + α), where R > 0. State the value of R.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the expression in part (a), find α in degrees, correct to 2 decimal places, where 0° < α < 90°.
parts.examinerComment: Some used tan α = 3/4, giving 36.87°.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2 sec²θ − 3 tan θ − 1 = 0 for 0° < θ < 90°. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for solving: tan θ = 1 or 1/2

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who did not use the identity could make no progress.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve y = x²e^({k}x) at the point where x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the product rule

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates forgot the factor of {k} when differentiating e^({k}x).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A curve has parametric equations x = t², y = {c}t³. Find dy/dx when t = {t}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered by those who remembered to divide in the right order.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of y = ln({a}x + {b}) at the point where x = 1.
parts.examinerComment: The numerator {a} was often missing.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of e^({k}x) from x = 0 to x = {u}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates evaluated (1/{k})e^({k}x) at the upper limit only, forgetting the lower limit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the exact value of the integral of 2/(2x + 1) from x = 0 to x = {u}, then give it correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using limits: ln {=2*u+1} − ln 1

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the trapezium rule with 2 intervals to estimate the integral of √(1 + x²) from x = 0 to x = {b}. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Using 2 intervals means h = {=b/2}. A common error was taking h = {b}.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show that the equation x³ − 2x − 5 = 0 has a root between x = 2 and x = 3.

markingPoints.text: M1 for evaluating f(2) = −1 and f(3) = 16
A1 for stating the sign change, so a root lies between 2 and 3

parts.examinerComment: A conclusion referring to the change of sign is required for the second mark.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = ∛(2xₙ + 5), with x₁ = 2, to find the root correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once
M1 for continuing until values agree to 3 d.p.

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should show each iterate to at least 5 decimal places.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Show that the equation ln x = 3 − x has a root between x = 2 and x = 3.

markingPoints.text: M1 for considering f(x) = ln x + x − 3 and evaluating f(2) ≈ −0.31 and f(3) ≈ 1.10

parts.examinerComment: Rearranging to f(x) = 0 first makes the sign change argument clearer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Expand (1 + 2x)^(−1/2) in ascending powers of x, up to and including the term in x².

markingPoints.text: M1 for the binomial form with n = −1/2

parts.examinerComment: The most common error was not squaring the 2 in the x² term.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Express (5x + 1) / ((x + 1)(x − 1)) in partial fractions.

markingPoints.text: M1 for A/(x + 1) + B/(x − 1) and a method to find A or B

parts.examinerComment: Substituting x = 1 and x = −1 was the quickest method.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the inequality |x − 2| < |2x + 1|.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who solved only x − 2 = 2x + 1 missed half the solution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2^(2x) − 5(2^x) + 6 = 0.

markingPoints.text: M1 for substituting u = 2^x to get u² − 5u + 6 = 0

parts.examinerComment: Recognising the hidden quadratic is the key step.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation ln(2x − 1) = {k}, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation {a}^(x + 1) = {b}^(2x), giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for taking logarithms: (x + 1) ln {a} = 2x ln {b}

parts.examinerComment: Errors in rearranging after taking logs were common.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation cos 2θ + 3 cos θ = 1 for 0° < θ < 360°.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should state why cos θ = −2 has no solutions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that tan A = 1/2 and tan B = 1/3, find the exact value of tan(A + B).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Express cos x − √3 sin x in the form R cos(x + α), where R > 0 and 0° < α < 90°. Give the exact values of R and α.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the gradient of y = x/(x + {a}) at the point where x = 1.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the quotient rule

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The curve x² + xy + y² = {=p^2+p*q+q^2} passes through ({p}, {q}). Find dy/dx at this point.
parts.examinerComment: The product rule on xy was the most common source of error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the exact coordinates of the stationary point on the curve y = xe^(−x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for product rule: e^(−x) − xe^(−x)

parts.examinerComment: Exact means leaving the answer as 1/e rather than 0.368.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of xeˣ from x = 0 to x = {u}, correct to 3 significant figures where appropriate.

markingPoints.text: M1 for integrating by parts with u = x
M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Choosing u = eˣ makes the integral harder. The lower limit contributes −(0 − 1) = +1, which was often lost.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of sin²x from x = 0 to x = π/2, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The double angle identity is essential here.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of 2x/(x² + 1) from x = 0 to x = {u}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for recognising the f'(x)/f(x) form

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use the iteration xₙ₊₁ = cos xₙ, with x₁ = 0.7 and x in radians, to find the root of x = cos x correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for at least one correct iterate

parts.examinerComment: Calculators in degree mode gave nonsense answers.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Show that the equation eˣ = 3 − x has a root between x = 0.7 and x = 0.8.

markingPoints.text: M1 for evaluating eˣ + x − 3 at both values: −0.286 and 0.026

parts.examinerComment: Values should be given to enough accuracy to show the sign.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Use the iteration xₙ₊₁ = ln(3 − xₙ), with x₁ = 0.8, to find this root correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the angle between the vectors a = {a1}i + {a2}j + {a3}k and b = {b1}i − {b2}j + {b3}k, in degrees, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A negative scalar product gives an obtuse angle, which is correct for the angle between the vectors.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The line l has equation r = (i + 2k) + t(2i + j − k). Find the value of t for which l passes through the point ({=1+2*t}, {t}, {=2-t}).

markingPoints.text: M1 for forming an equation in t from one component
A1 for t = {t}, checked in all three components

parts.examinerComment: All three components should be checked.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Lines l₁: r = (i + j) + s(i + k) and l₂: r = (2i + 3k) + t(j + k). Determine whether the lines intersect, are parallel, or are skew.

markingPoints.text: B1 for stating the directions are not parallel
M1 for equating components: 1 + s = 2, 1 = t, s = 3 + t
A1 for s = 1, t = 1 from two equations
A1 for showing the third equation fails (1 ≠ 4), so the lines are skew

parts.examinerComment: To show lines are skew, you must show they are not parallel and do not intersect.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Solve dy/dx = {k}xy, given that y = 1 when x = 0. Find y when x = {a}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for separating variables: ∫ 1/y dy = ∫ {k}x dx
M1 for using y = 1 at x = 0

parts.examinerComment: Missing the constant of integration made it impossible to use the initial condition.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Solve dy/dx = (y + 1)/x for x > 0, given that y = {c} when x = 1. Find y when x = {a}.

markingPoints.text: A1 for ln(y + 1) = ln x + c

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who combined logs carefully reached y + 1 = {=c+1}x efficiently.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The temperature θ °C of a cooling liquid decreases at a rate proportional to (θ − 20). Write down a differential equation relating θ and time t.

markingPoints.text: B1 for dθ/dt = k(θ − 20) with a constant
B1 for a negative sign or a statement that k < 0 for a decrease

parts.examinerComment: The sign of the constant must reflect that the temperature decreases.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the modulus of the complex number z = {a} + {b}i.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Express (2 + i)/(1 − i) in the form x + iy.

markingPoints.text: M1 for multiplying numerator and denominator by 1 + i

parts.examinerComment: Multiplying by the conjugate of the denominator is the standard method.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Solve the equation z² + 4z + 13 = 0.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the quadratic formula or completing the square

parts.examinerComment: Both roots are required.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A particle of mass {m} kg rests on a smooth plane inclined at {th}° to the horizontal. It is held in equilibrium by a force P N acting up the plane, parallel to it. Find P.

markingPoints.text: M1 for resolving parallel to the plane: P = {m}g sin {th}°

parts.examinerComment: Use g = 10 m s⁻². Resolving vertically instead of along the plane was a common error.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A box of mass {m} kg rests on rough horizontal ground. The coefficient of friction is {mu}. Find the least horizontal force needed to move the box, in N.

markingPoints.text: M1 for F = μR with R = {=10*m}

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Forces of {a} N and {b} N act at right angles on a particle. Find the magnitude of the third force needed to keep it in equilibrium, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A car accelerates uniformly from {u} m s⁻¹ to {v} m s⁻¹ in {t} s. Find the distance travelled, in m.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A stone is thrown vertically upwards at {u} m s⁻¹. Find its greatest height above the point of projection, in m.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used g = 9.8; the syllabus uses g = 10.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with velocity v = 3t² − {=3*a}t m s⁻¹ at time t s. Find the distance travelled between t = 0 and t = {T}, in m.
parts.examinerComment: The displacement is −{=1.5*a*T^2 - T^3} m because v < 0 throughout; the question asks for distance, which is positive.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A particle of mass {m1} kg moving at {u} m s⁻¹ collides with a particle of mass {m2} kg at rest. They coalesce. Find their common speed, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A 2 kg particle moving at 6 m s⁻¹ collides directly with a 4 kg particle moving at 1 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction. After the collision the 2 kg particle moves at 2 m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction to its original motion. Find the speed of the 4 kg particle after the collision, in m s⁻¹.

markingPoints.text: M1 for conservation of momentum with correct signs

parts.examinerComment: Choosing a positive direction and sticking to it avoids sign errors.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For the collision in part (a), find the loss of kinetic energy, in J.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A horizontal force of {F} N acts on a particle of mass {m} kg on a smooth horizontal surface. Find its acceleration, in m s⁻².
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A lift of mass {m} kg accelerates upwards at {a} m s⁻². Find the tension in the cable, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates omitted the weight.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Particles of mass {=m2+d} kg and {m2} kg are connected by a light inextensible string over a smooth fixed pulley and released from rest. Find the acceleration of the particles, in m s⁻².

markingPoints.text: M1 for an equation of motion for one particle
M1 for a second equation or the whole system: {=m2+d}g − {m2}g = {=2*m2+d}a

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A force of {F} N acting at {th}° above the horizontal pulls a box {d} m along horizontal ground. Find the work done by the force, in J.
parts.examinerComment: Only the component in the direction of motion does work.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A car's engine works at {P} kW while the car moves at a constant {v} m s⁻¹ on a level road. Find the resistance to motion, in N.
parts.examinerComment: Converting kW to W was essential.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A particle is released from rest at the top of a smooth slope of vertical height {h} m. Find its speed at the bottom, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the interquartile range of the data 3, 7, 7, 9, 12, 14, 18.

markingPoints.text: B1 for lower quartile 7 and upper quartile 14

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For 10 values, Σx = {S} and Σx² = {Q}. Find the standard deviation, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some forgot to square root the variance.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: In a histogram, the class 10 ≤ x < {=10+w} has frequency {f}. Find its frequency density.
parts.examinerComment: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the number of different arrangements of the letters of the word LETTER.
parts.examinerComment: Both repeated letters (E and T) must be accounted for.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A committee of 4 is chosen from {m} men and {w} women. In how many ways can it be chosen with exactly 2 women?
parts.examinerComment: Adding instead of multiplying was a common error.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: In how many ways can {n} people sit in a row if two particular people must sit next to each other?
parts.examinerComment: Treating the pair as one unit is the key idea.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Events A and B are independent, with P(A) = {a} and P(B) = {b}. Find P(A ∪ B).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown. Find the probability that the total is 8. Give your answer as a fraction.
parts.examinerComment: A sample space diagram helps.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: P(A ∩ B) = {=b*c} and P(B) = {b}. Find P(A | B).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ B({n}, {p}). Find P(X = {r}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The probability of success in each trial is {p}. Find the probability that the first success occurs on the {k}th trial.
parts.examinerComment: This is a geometric distribution.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: A random variable X takes values 1, 2 and 3 with probabilities {p1}, {p2} and {=1-p1-p2}. Find E(X).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ N({mu}, {=s^2}). Find P(X < {=mu+d}), correct to 4 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Dividing by the variance ({=s^2}) instead of the standard deviation ({s}) was the most common error.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: X ~ N(μ, {=s^2}) and P(X > {x}) = 0.1. Find μ, correct to 4 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: X ~ B({n}, {p}). Use a suitable normal approximation to find P(X ≥ {=n*p+c}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Omitting the continuity correction lost a mark.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ Po({l}). Find P(X = {r}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: X ~ Po({l}). Find P(X ≤ 1), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Emails arrive at random at an average rate of {R} per hour. Find the probability that exactly {r} arrive in a {M}-minute period, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The rate must be scaled to the time period.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: X ~ N(10, 4) and Y ~ N(15, 9) are independent. Find Var(2X − Y).
parts.examinerComment: Variances add, even when the variables are subtracted.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For the X in part (a), find E(3X + 2).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For X and Y in part (a), find P(X + Y > 28), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = kx² for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, and 0 otherwise. Find k.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ kx² dx from 0 to 3 = 1

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: For this distribution, find E(X).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find the median of X, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ from 0 to m of x²/9 dx = 0.5

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A random sample of 50 values gives Σx = {S} and Σx² = {Q}. Find an unbiased estimate of the population variance, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Dividing by n instead of n − 1 lost marks.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: A random sample of 64 values from a population with standard deviation 4 has mean 25. Find a 95% confidence interval for the population mean.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: X ~ N({mu}, {=s^2}). A random sample of {=k^2} values is taken. Find the probability that the sample mean exceeds {=mu+d}, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The variance of the sample mean is σ²/n.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: A coin is thought to be biased towards heads. State suitable null and alternative hypotheses for a test, where p is the probability of a head.
parts.examinerComment: Hypotheses must be stated in terms of the parameter p.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: The coin is thrown 20 times and shows 15 heads. Assuming H₀, find P(X ≥ 15), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Carry out the test at the 5% significance level, stating your conclusion in context.

markingPoints.text: A1 for rejecting H₀: there is evidence that the coin is biased towards heads

parts.examinerComment: Conclusions must be in context and should not be stated as certain.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the constant k for which the equation x² + {b}x + k = 0 has two equal real roots.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates recognised that equal roots require a zero discriminant. A few set the discriminant greater than zero, which gives two distinct roots.

parts.prompt: By expressing x² − {=2*p}x + {c} in the form (x − a)² + b, find the minimum value of x² − {=2*p}x + {c}.
parts.examinerComment: Stronger answers stated the minimum value directly from the completed-square form. Some candidates gave the x-coordinate of the minimum point ({p}) instead of the minimum value.

parts.prompt: Solve the inequality 2x² − 5x − 12 > 0.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the critical values correctly. A sketch of the parabola helped candidates choose the correct outer regions; giving −3/2 < x < 4 was a common error.

parts.prompt: Find the set of values of m for which the line y = mx − 3 does not meet the curve y = x² + x + 1. Show your working.

markingPoints.text: M1 for equating and rearranging: x² + (1 − m)x + 4 = 0
M1 for using the discriminant: (1 − m)² − 16 < 0
A1 for critical values m = −3 and m = 5

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who rearranged to a quadratic equal to zero before using the discriminant were usually successful. Weaker answers used b² − 4ac > 0 or left the answer as two separate inequalities without the correct link.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation x⁴ − {=a^2+b^2}x² + {=a^2*b^2} = 0. Give the largest root.

markingPoints.text: M1 for treating as a quadratic in x²: (x² − {=a^2})(x² − {=b^2}) = 0

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who substituted u = x² handled this well. Some stopped at u = {=b^2} and gave this as the answer.

parts.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x) = {a}x + {b} for x ∈ ℝ. Find the value of f⁻¹({c}).
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates solved f(x) = {c} directly. A common error was to calculate 1/f({c}).

parts.prompt: The functions f and g are defined for x ∈ ℝ by f(x) = x² + {p} and g(x) = {q}x − 1. Find the value of gf({r}).
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found fg({r}) = {=(q*r-1)^2+p} instead. gf means apply f first.

parts.prompt:
The function f is defined by f(x) = 2x² − 8x + 5 for x ≥ k.
(i) Express f(x) in the form a(x + b)² + c.
(ii) State the least value of k for which f has an inverse.
(iii) For this value of k, find an expression for f⁻¹(x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for making x the subject of y = 2(x − 2)² − 3

parts.examinerComment: The completed-square form shows the vertex at (2, −3), so the function is one-one for x ≥ 2. Many candidates gave 2 ± √((x + 3)/2) and lost the final mark: the negative root does not apply on this domain.

parts.prompt: The graph of y = f(x) is transformed to the graph of y = f(x − 3) + 2. Describe fully the single transformation.

markingPoints.text: B1 for vector (3, 2), i.e. 3 units in the positive x-direction and 2 in the positive y-direction

parts.examinerComment: The word 'translation' is required; 'shift' or 'move' was not accepted. A common error was a horizontal movement of 3 units to the left.

parts.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x) = {a}x² − {b} for −1 ≤ x ≤ {c}. Find the greatest value of f(x).

markingPoints.text: M1 for recognising the greatest value occurs at x = {c}

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who sketched the graph saw that the greatest value occurs at the end of the domain furthest from 0.

parts.prompt: The points A and B have coordinates ({a}, {b}) and ({=a+p}, {=b+q}). Find the length of AB.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: The line L passes through the point ({a}, {b}) and is perpendicular to the line y = {m}x + 3. Find the y-coordinate of the point where L crosses the y-axis.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the perpendicular gradient. Errors in the sign when substituting x = 0 were common.

parts.prompt: The line y = {=2*m}x + k is a tangent to the curve y = x² + {c}. Find the value of k.
parts.examinerComment: Using a repeated root (discriminant zero) is the standard method for tangency. Some candidates differentiated instead, which also works if completed correctly.

parts.prompt: The points A(1, 3) and B(7, −1) are joined. Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB, giving your answer in the form ax + by = c.

markingPoints.text: M1 for perpendicular gradient 3/2 used with their midpoint

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the midpoint correctly. Using the gradient of AB rather than the perpendicular gradient was the most common error.

parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points of intersection of the curve y = x² − 3x + 4 and the line y = 2x − 2.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A few candidates gave only the x-coordinates.

parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius {r} cm and angle {t} radians. Find the perimeter of the sector, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: The perimeter includes both radii. A significant number of candidates gave the arc length only.

parts.prompt: A sector of a circle has radius {r} cm and area {=0.5*r^2*t} cm². Find the length of the arc of the sector, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the angle first. The formula area = ½ × r × arc length gives the answer in one step.

parts.prompt: A chord of a circle of radius {r} cm subtends an angle of {t} radians at the centre. Find the area of the minor segment cut off by the chord, in cm², correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for subtracting triangle area ½ × {r}² × sin {t}

parts.examinerComment: Calculators must be in radian mode. Candidates who used sin {t}° gave answers that were far too large.

parts.prompt: Points A and B lie on a circle with centre O and radius {r} cm. The chord AB has length {c} cm. Find angle AOB in radians, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for sin(½θ) = {=c/2}/{r} or use of the cosine rule

parts.examinerComment: Splitting the isosceles triangle into two right-angled triangles is efficient. Some candidates forgot to double the half-angle.

parts.prompt: A sector has radius 9 cm and angle 2π/3 radians. Find the exact perimeter of the sector, in cm.
parts.examinerComment: An exact answer must be left in terms of π. Decimal answers (36.8) did not gain the final mark.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2 sin²θ + 3 cos θ = 0 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.

markingPoints.text: M1 for solving: cos θ = −1/2 (cos θ = 2 rejected)

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates used the correct identity. Weaker answers did not reject cos θ = 2 explicitly or missed the second solution in the third quadrant.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation sin θ = {k} for 0° < θ < 180°. Give the larger solution, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: The second solution is 180° minus the principal value. Many candidates gave only the calculator value.

parts.prompt: Prove the identity tan θ + 1/tan θ ≡ 1/(sin θ cos θ).

markingPoints.text: M1 for writing tan θ = sin θ/cos θ
M1 for combining: (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sin θ cos θ)
A1 for using sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 to complete the proof

parts.examinerComment: Proofs should start from one side and reach the other. Candidates who worked on both sides at once were not given full credit.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation tan 2x = {k} for 0° < x < 180°. Give the larger solution, correct to 1 decimal place.

markingPoints.text: M1 for adding 180° to 2x before halving

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must find all values of 2x in the range 0° < 2x < 360° before dividing by 2. Adding 180° to x instead of to 2x was a common error.

parts.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x) = {a} − {b} cos 2x for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. State the greatest value of f(x).
parts.examinerComment: This occurs where cos 2x = −1, at x = π/2. Some candidates gave {=a-b}, the least value.

parts.prompt: In an arithmetic progression the 5th term is {=a+4*d} and the 12th term is {=a+11*d}. Find the sum of the first 20 terms.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates set up the simultaneous equations correctly. Some used 20d instead of 19d in the sum formula.

parts.prompt: A geometric progression with positive terms has first term {a} and third term {=a*r^2}. Find the sum to infinity.
parts.examinerComment: Since the terms are positive, the positive square root is taken. Some candidates used r = {=r^2}.

parts.prompt: Find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (1 + {k}x)({a} + x)⁵.

markingPoints.text: B1 for x term of ({a} + x)⁵: {=5*a^4}x
B1 for x² term of ({a} + x)⁵: {=10*a^3}x²

parts.examinerComment: Candidates need two terms of the expansion. Those who expanded only up to x² and then multiplied out carefully scored well.

parts.prompt: Find the term independent of x in the expansion of (x + {a}/x²)⁶.

markingPoints.text: M1 for general term ⁶Cᵣ x^(6 − r)({a}/x²)^r and 6 − 3r = 0

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should find the power of x in a general term rather than writing out the whole expansion.

parts.prompt:
A geometric progression has sum to infinity equal to three times its first term. The second term is 12.
Find the common ratio and the first term.
parts.examinerComment: Cancelling a from a/(1 − r) = 3a was the key step. Some candidates confused the second term with the first.

parts.prompt: The normal to the curve y = x² + {c} at the point where x = {p} meets the x-axis at Q. Find the x-coordinate of Q.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the gradient of the normal. Errors in rearranging after setting y = 0 were common.

parts.prompt: The curve y = x³ − {=3*a^2}x + {c} has a minimum point. Find the y-coordinate of the minimum point.

markingPoints.text: M1 for d²y/dx² = 6x > 0 at x = {a}, so minimum

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must justify which stationary point is the minimum. Some substituted x = −{a}, giving the maximum.

parts.prompt: The radius of a circle is increasing at a constant rate of {k} cm s⁻¹. Find the rate of increase of the area of the circle when the radius is {r} cm, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Candidates should set out the chain rule explicitly.

parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve y = √({a}x + {b}) at the point where x = {c}, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The factor {a} from the chain rule was sometimes omitted.

parts.prompt: The function f is defined by f(x) = x³ + 3x² + kx for x ∈ ℝ. Find the set of values of the constant k for which f is an increasing function.

markingPoints.text: M1 for requiring f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x: 36 − 12k ≤ 0

parts.examinerComment: An increasing function has f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x, so the quadratic f'(x) must have no real roots (or a repeated root). Some candidates solved f'(x) = 0 with a particular value of x instead.

parts.prompt: A curve has gradient dy/dx = {a}x² − {b} and passes through the point (1, {c}). Find the value of y when x = 2.
parts.examinerComment: Omitting the constant of integration made it impossible to use the given point.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of {a}/x² with respect to x, from x = 1 to x = {k}.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Writing the integrand as {a}x⁻² before integrating avoided most errors.

parts.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by the curve y = x² and the line y = {k}x.

markingPoints.text: B1 for intersections at x = 0 and x = {k}

parts.examinerComment: Subtracting the curve from the line gave a positive area directly.

parts.prompt: The region bounded by the curve y = {a}/x, the x-axis and the lines x = 1 and x = {b} is rotated through 360° about the x-axis. Find the volume of the solid formed, as a multiple of π. Enter the multiple only.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: The volume formula requires y². Candidates who integrated {a}/x did not reach a valid method.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of (2x + {a})³ with respect to x, from x = 0 to x = 1.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates remembered to divide by 4 but forgot to divide by the derivative of the bracket, 2.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation |2x − 3| = |x + 4|.

markingPoints.text: M1 for squaring both sides or considering 2x − 3 = ±(x + 4)

parts.examinerComment: Squaring both sides gives 3x² − 20x − 7 = 0, which factorises. Some candidates found only x = 7.

parts.prompt: Solve the inequality |x − 3| < 2|x|.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who squared both sides usually found the critical values. Checking a value in each region, such as x = 0, confirms which regions satisfy the inequality.

parts.prompt: Find the remainder when 2x³ + {a}x² − x + {b} is divided by (2x − 1).
parts.examinerComment: Substituting x = 2 or x = −½ were the common errors. The remainder theorem uses the root of 2x − 1 = 0.

parts.prompt: The polynomial p(x) = x³ + ax² + bx − 6 has a factor (x − 1). When p(x) is divided by (x + 1) the remainder is {r}. Find the value of a.
parts.examinerComment: Sign errors when substituting x = −1 into x³ and bx were the main source of lost marks.

parts.prompt: Find the quotient and remainder when x³ − 2x² + 4x + 1 is divided by x² + x − 1.

markingPoints.text: M1 for a correct division method reaching a linear quotient

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who wrote the identity x³ − 2x² + 4x + 1 ≡ (x² + x − 1)(x + c) + dx + e and compared coefficients were as successful as those using long division.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2^(2x) − {=a+b} × 2ˣ + {=a*b} = 0. Give the larger root correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for recognising a quadratic in u = 2ˣ: u² − {=a+b}u + {=a*b} = 0

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who wrote 2^(2x) = (2ˣ)² were usually successful.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation ln x + ln(x + {a}) = ln {b}. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: A1 for rejecting the negative root

parts.examinerComment: The negative root must be rejected because ln x is undefined for x ≤ 0.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation {a}e^(2x) = {b}, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates took logarithms before dividing by {a} and wrote ln {a} × 2x, a misuse of the laws of logarithms.

parts.prompt: The variables x and y satisfy y = Axⁿ. The graph of ln y against ln x is a straight line passing through the points (1.2, {q}) and (3.2, {s}). Find the value of n.

markingPoints.text: B1 for ln y = ln A + n ln x

parts.examinerComment: The gradient of the line is n. Some candidates found the gradient correctly but then gave eⁿ.

parts.prompt: Given that ln x = p and ln y = q, express ln(x³/√y) in terms of p and q.

markingPoints.text: M1 for 3 ln x − ½ ln y

parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A few candidates wrote ln √y = √q.

parts.prompt: Find the least value of {c} + {a} cos θ − {b} sin θ as θ varies.

markingPoints.text: M1 for expressing {a} cos θ − {b} sin θ as R cos(θ + α)

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who used the R cos(θ + α) form recognised that the least value occurs when the cosine is −1.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation sec²θ = 3 tan θ − 1 for 0° < θ < 180°.

markingPoints.text: M1 for solving: tan θ = 1 or tan θ = 2

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates used the correct identity. A few gave extra solutions in the second quadrant, where tan θ is negative.

parts.prompt: Given that sin A = {s}, find the value of cos 2A.
parts.examinerComment: Choosing the form of cos 2A involving sin A avoids having to find cos A.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2 sin 2θ = {k} cos θ for 0° < θ < 90°, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ
M1 for factorising: cos θ(4 sin θ − {k}) = 0

parts.examinerComment: Dividing by cos θ is valid here because cos θ ≠ 0 in the given range, but candidates should say so.

parts.prompt: Express tan(θ + 45°) in terms of t, where t = tan θ.

markingPoints.text: M1 for (tan θ + tan 45°)/(1 − tan θ tan 45°)

parts.examinerComment: Well answered by candidates who recalled tan 45° = 1.

parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve y = e^(2x)/(x + {a}) at the point where x = 0.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the quotient rule

parts.examinerComment: Errors in the order of terms in the numerator of the quotient rule were the most common.

parts.prompt: The curve x² + {a}y² = {=p^2 + a*q^2} passes through the point ({p}, {q}). Find dy/dx at this point.
parts.examinerComment: Most candidates differentiated y² correctly using the chain rule.

parts.prompt: The curve y = x²e^(−x/{k}) has a stationary point other than the origin. Find its y-coordinate, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the product rule

parts.examinerComment: The factor −1/{k} from differentiating the exponential was sometimes lost.

parts.prompt: A curve has parametric equations x = {a} cos t, y = {b} sin t. Find dy/dx at the point where t = π/6, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for dx/dt = −{a} sin t and dy/dt = {b} cos t

parts.examinerComment: The negative sign from differentiating cos t was frequently lost.

parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of the stationary point of the curve y = x ln x − {a}x, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the product rule on x ln x

parts.examinerComment: Well answered. A few candidates differentiated x ln x as 1/x.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of ({a}e^(−x) + {b}) with respect to x, from x = 0 to x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: The sign of the integral of e^(−x) caused difficulty for some candidates.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of (2x + {a}/x) with respect to x, from x = 1 to x = {k}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates integrated correctly. Some forgot that ln 1 = 0 only after substituting the lower limit.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of (sec²x + {a} sin x) with respect to x, from x = 0 to x = π/3, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for tan x − {a} cos x
M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who integrated sin x as cos x lost the accuracy marks.

parts.prompt: Use the trapezium rule with 3 intervals to estimate the integral of 1/(1 + x²) from x = 0 to x = {=3*h}. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Three intervals require four ordinates. Some candidates used only three.

parts.prompt: Find ∫ (e^(2x) + 1)² dx.
parts.examinerComment: The bracket must be expanded before integrating. A common error was (e^(2x) + 1)³/3.

parts.prompt: Show by calculation that the equation x³ − 5x + 1 = 0 has a root between x = 2 and x = 2.5.

markingPoints.text: M1 for evaluating f(2) = −1 and f(2.5) = 4.125
A1 for stating the sign change implies a root

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must state the conclusion, referring to the change of sign and the continuity of the function.

parts.prompt: The equation x³ − {a}x − 1 = 0 has a positive root. Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = ∛({a}xₙ + 1), with x₁ = 2, to find this root correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once
M1 for continuing until values agree to 3 d.p.

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should record each iterate to at least 5 decimal places.

parts.prompt: Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = {c} + ln xₙ, with x₁ = {=c+1}, to find the root of x = {c} + ln x that is greater than 1, correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once
M1 for continuing until values agree to 3 d.p.

parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Stronger answers showed the final two iterates agreeing to 3 decimal places.

parts.prompt: Show that the equation x³ + 2x − 7 = 0 can be written in the form x = √(7/x − 2), for x > 0.

markingPoints.text: M1 for x³ = 7 − 2x and dividing by x: x² = 7/x − 2
A1 for taking the positive square root, x > 0

parts.examinerComment: Show-that questions require every step. Some candidates started from the given answer and worked backwards without making the logic clear.

parts.prompt: The sequence defined by xₙ₊₁ = (2xₙ³ + {a})/(3xₙ²), with x₁ = 2, converges to α. Find α correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once
M1 for α satisfying α = (2α³ + {a})/(3α²), i.e. α³ = {a}

parts.examinerComment: Stronger candidates recognised that α = ∛{a} and used this to confirm their iterates.

parts.prompt: Find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of (1 − {a}x)^(1/2) in ascending powers of x.
parts.examinerComment: Many candidates wrote (−{a}x)² as −{=a^2}x², giving the wrong sign.

parts.prompt: Find the coefficient of x² in the expansion of √(4 + {a}x) in ascending powers of x.

markingPoints.text: M1 for taking out the factor 2: 2(1 + {a}x/4)^(1/2)

parts.examinerComment: Candidates must take out the factor of 4 as 2, not 4. Some forgot to multiply by 2 at the end.

parts.prompt: Express (5x + 1)/((x − 1)(x + 2)) in partial fractions.
parts.examinerComment: Substituting x = 1 and x = −2 gives the constants immediately.

parts.prompt: Express (3x² + x + 2)/((x + 1)(x − 1)²) in partial fractions.

markingPoints.text: B1 for the form A/(x + 1) + B/(x − 1) + C/(x − 1)²

parts.examinerComment: The repeated factor needs both B/(x − 1) and C/(x − 1)². Comparing the coefficients of x² gives B once A is known.

parts.prompt: Solve the inequality |3x − 1| > |x + 3|.

markingPoints.text: M1 for squaring both sides: 9x² − 6x + 1 > x² + 6x + 9

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the critical values. Some gave the inside region −½ < x < 2.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation 2 ln x = ln(x + {a}) + ln 3, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: A1 for rejecting the negative root

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who combined the logarithms correctly were usually successful. The negative root must be rejected.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation 4ˣ = 3 × 2ˣ + {=k^2 - 3*k}, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should give a reason for rejecting the negative value of 2ˣ.

parts.prompt: The variables x and y satisfy y = Abˣ. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line passing through (1, {p}) and (4, {q}). Find the value of b, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for ln y = ln A + x ln b

parts.examinerComment: The gradient is ln b, not b. Several candidates gave {=(q-p)/3} as the answer.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation |2ˣ − {a}| = 3. Give the larger root correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Both cases of the modulus need considering, but only the larger root was asked for.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation ln(2x + 3) = 2 ln x + ln 3, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using laws of logarithms: 2x + 3 = 3x²
A1 for rejecting the negative root since ln x requires x > 0

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates combined the logarithms correctly. Few justified rejecting the negative root.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation {a} cos θ + {b} sin θ = {c} for 0° < θ < 180°. Give the largest solution in this interval, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: Writing the left-hand side as R cos(θ − α) is the efficient method. The value of θ from θ − α = −{=round(acos(c/sqrt(a^2+b^2))*180/pi, 2)}° is smaller, or lies outside the interval.

parts.prompt: Prove the identity sin 2θ/(1 + cos 2θ) ≡ tan θ.

markingPoints.text: B1 for sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ
B1 for simplifying to tan θ

parts.examinerComment: Choosing cos 2θ = 2cos²θ − 1 makes the denominator a single term.

parts.prompt: Given that tan A = {p} and tan B = {q}, find the value of tan(A − B).
parts.examinerComment: A sign error in the denominator was the most common mistake.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation cos 2θ + 3 sin θ = 2 for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°.

markingPoints.text: M1 for sin θ = ½ or sin θ = 1

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates missed θ = 90° from sin θ = 1.

parts.prompt: Solve the equation tan 2θ = {k} tan θ for 0° < θ < 90°, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

markingPoints.text: M1 for 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ) = {k} tan θ
M1 for cancelling tan θ ≠ 0: 1 − tan²θ = {=2/k}

parts.examinerComment: Candidates should note that tan θ = 0 gives no solution in the open interval.

parts.prompt: Find the gradient of the curve y = x/√(x² + {a}) at the point where x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for the quotient or product rule
A1 for dy/dx = {a}/(x² + {a})^(3/2) or unsimplified equivalent

parts.examinerComment: Simplifying before substituting x = 1 reduced arithmetic errors.

parts.prompt: A curve has parametric equations x = ln(t + {a}), y = t². Find dy/dx when t = {p}.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: The curve y³ + {a}xy = x² + {a} passes through the point (1, 1). Find dy/dx at this point.
parts.examinerComment: The product rule on {a}xy was the main source of error.

parts.prompt: Find the x-coordinate of the stationary point of the curve y = ln x/x^{k}, for x > 0, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: A1 for numerator x^{=k-1}(1 − {k} ln x)

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who simplified the numerator before setting it to zero were most successful.

parts.prompt: The curve y = eˣ sin x is defined for 0 ≤ x ≤ π. Find the exact x-coordinate of the stationary point and determine whether it is a maximum or a minimum.

markingPoints.text: M1 for the product rule: eˣ sin x + eˣ cos x
M1 for setting sin x + cos x = 0: tan x = −1
M1 for a valid method to determine the nature, e.g. d²y/dx² = 2eˣ cos x < 0

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates divided by eˣ without comment; this is valid since eˣ > 0. Answers in degrees were not exact.

parts.prompt: Use the substitution u = x² + 1 to find the value of the integral of x(x² + 1)^{n} from x = 0 to x = 1, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ½ ∫ u^{n} du with limits 1 and 2

parts.examinerComment: Changing the limits to values of u avoided substituting back. Some candidates used the original limits for u.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of x ln x from x = 1 to x = {k}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for integration by parts with u = ln x
A1 for ½x² ln x − ∫ ½x dx
A1 for ½x² ln x − ¼x²
M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Choosing u = x leads to integrating ln x, which is harder. The lower limit gives −(0 − ¼).

parts.prompt: By first expressing 1/((x − 1)(x + 1)) in partial fractions, find the value of the integral of 1/((x − 1)(x + 1)) from x = 2 to x = {k}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: A1 for ½ ln(x − 1) − ½ ln(x + 1)
M1 for correct use of limits

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates found the partial fractions. Combining the logarithms at the end needed care.

parts.prompt: Find the value of the integral of ({a} + tan²x) from x = 0 to x = π/4, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The identity tan²x = sec²x − 1 is essential; tan²x cannot be integrated directly.

parts.prompt: Use the substitution u = √x to find ∫ 1/(x + √x) dx.
parts.examinerComment: The answer must be in terms of x. Some candidates forgot to replace dx.

parts.prompt: The sequence defined by xₙ₊₁ = ½(xₙ + {a}/xₙ), with x₁ = 3, converges to α. State an equation satisfied by α and find α correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: B1 for α = ½(α + {a}/α), i.e. α² = {a}
M1 for using the iteration correctly

parts.examinerComment: Stronger candidates recognised α = √{a} and used the iterates to confirm it.

parts.prompt: The equation x = {k}e^(−x) has one real root. Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = {k}e^(−xₙ), with x₁ = 0.5, to find the root correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once

parts.examinerComment: The iterates oscillate about the root, so candidates needed several more iterations than usual.

parts.prompt: Show by calculation that the equation ln x = 3 − x has a root between x = 2 and x = 2.5.

markingPoints.text: M1 for considering f(x) = ln x + x − 3: f(2) = −0.307, f(2.5) = 0.416
A1 for the sign change and conclusion

parts.examinerComment: Values should be given to at least 2 significant figures and the conclusion stated clearly.

parts.prompt: Show that if the sequence xₙ₊₁ = ⅓(2xₙ + 7/xₙ²) converges, then it converges to ∛7.

markingPoints.text: M1 for setting xₙ₊₁ = xₙ = α: 3α = 2α + 7/α²

parts.examinerComment: Well answered by candidates who replaced both iterates by the limit α.

parts.prompt: Use the iterative formula xₙ₊₁ = ∛(xₙ + {a}), with x₁ = 2, to find the real root of x³ − x − {a} = 0 correct to 3 decimal places.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the iteration correctly at least once

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Relative to the origin O, the points A and B have position vectors i + {p}j − 2k and {q}i + 3j + k. Find |AB|, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found OA + OB instead of OB − OA.

parts.prompt: The vector pi + 2j − k is perpendicular to the vector 3i − {a}j + {b}k. Find the value of p.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: The lines l and m have equations r = (i + 2j + 3k) + s(i − j + 2k) and r = (4i + 5k) + t(2i + j − k). Show that l and m are skew.

markingPoints.text: B1 for the directions are not parallel
M1 for forming three equations: 1 + s = 4 + 2t, 2 − s = t, 3 + 2s = 5 − t
A1 for s = 7/3, t = −1/3 from two equations
A1 for showing the third equation is not satisfied, so the lines are skew

parts.examinerComment: Both conditions are needed: the lines must not intersect and must not be parallel.

parts.prompt: The line l passes through the origin and has direction i + 2j + 2k. Find the perpendicular distance from the point P({p}, {q}, 0) to l, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for a general point (t, 2t, 2t) on l

parts.examinerComment: Finding the foot of the perpendicular first was the most reliable method.

parts.prompt: Find the acute angle between the lines with directions i + {a}j + 2k and 2i − j + {b}k, in degrees, correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.examinerComment: If the scalar product is negative, the acute angle is found from its modulus.

parts.prompt: The variable y satisfies dy/dx = {k}y, and y = {y0} when x = 0. Find y when x = 2, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = x/y, given that y = {a} when x = 0 and y > 0. Find y when x = {b}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ y dy = ∫ x dx
M1 for using the condition: y² = x² + {=a^2}

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found the constant after taking square roots term by term, which is invalid.

parts.prompt: The temperature θ °C of a liquid satisfies dθ/dt = −{k}(θ − 20), where t is the time in minutes. When t = 0, θ = {T}. Find the time taken for the temperature to fall to 40 °C, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who wrote the solution in exponential form before substituting θ = 40 made fewer errors.

parts.prompt: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = e^(2x − y), given that y = 0 when x = 0. Give y in terms of x.

markingPoints.text: M1 for separating: ∫ eʸ dy = ∫ e^(2x) dx
M1 for using the condition: c = ½

parts.examinerComment: Writing e^(2x − y) = e^(2x)/eʸ was the key first step.

parts.prompt: A substance decays so that its mass m grams at time t days decreases at a rate proportional to the square root of m. Write down a differential equation relating m and t, using k for a positive constant.
parts.examinerComment: The negative sign shows that the mass is decreasing; it was often omitted.

parts.prompt: Find the modulus of the complex number ({a} + {b}i)({c} − {d}i), correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂| or for multiplying out

parts.examinerComment: Using |z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂| was quicker than expanding.

parts.prompt: Find the argument of the complex number −{a} + {b}i, in radians, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for a sketch or statement that the point is in the second quadrant

parts.examinerComment: A calculator gives tan⁻¹(−{b}/{a}), which is in the wrong quadrant. A sketch helps to avoid this.

parts.prompt: Express (5 + i)/(1 − i) in the form x + iy, where x and y are real.

markingPoints.text: M1 for multiplying numerator and denominator by 1 + i

parts.examinerComment: Well answered. Some candidates used i² = 1.

parts.prompt: Given that 1 + 2i is a root of the equation z³ − z² + 3z + 5 = 0, find the other two roots.

markingPoints.text: M1 for the quadratic factor z² − 2z + 5
M1 for dividing to find the linear factor z + 1

parts.examinerComment: Most candidates stated the conjugate root. Forming the quadratic factor from the sum and product of the roots was efficient.

parts.prompt: The complex number z satisfies |z − ({a} + {b}i)| = {r}. Find the least possible value of |z|, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for a circle with centre ({a}, {b}) and radius {r}
M1 for distance from O to centre = √{=a^2+b^2}

parts.examinerComment: A sketch on an Argand diagram showed that the least value lies on the line through the origin and the centre.

parts.prompt: A particle rests on a rough plane inclined at {th}° to the horizontal and is about to slip down the plane. Find the coefficient of friction, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for resolving perpendicular to the plane: R = mg cos {th}°
M1 for F = μR = mg sin {th}°

parts.examinerComment: The mass cancels, so no value of m is needed. Candidates who introduced a mass usually still succeeded.

parts.prompt: Two forces of magnitudes {a} N and {b} N act on a particle. The angle between their directions is 60°. Find the magnitude of their resultant, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for resolving both forces in two perpendicular directions

parts.examinerComment: Using the cosine rule with the angle 120° in the triangle of forces is an equally valid method.

parts.prompt: A particle of mass {m} kg hangs in equilibrium, supported by two light strings. One string makes an angle of {al}° with the horizontal and the other makes an angle of {be}° with the horizontal, on the other side. Find the tension in the string at {al}°, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for resolving horizontally: T₁ cos {al}° = T₂ cos {be}°
M1 for resolving vertically: T₁ sin {al}° + T₂ sin {be}° = {=10*m}

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates resolved correctly but made errors when eliminating T₂. Lami's theorem is an alternative.

parts.prompt: A box of mass {m} kg rests on rough horizontal ground, with coefficient of friction {mu}. A force of P N acting at {th}° above the horizontal is just sufficient to make the box move. Find P, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for resolving vertically: R = {=10*m} − P sin {th}°
M1 for resolving horizontally: P cos {th}° = F
A1 for a correct equation in P

parts.examinerComment: The normal reaction is reduced by the vertical component of P. Many candidates used R = {=10*m}.

parts.prompt: A particle of weight 20 N is placed on a rough plane inclined at 25° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the particle and the plane is 0.3. Determine whether the particle will remain at rest.

markingPoints.text: M1 for component of weight down the plane 20 sin 25° = 8.45 N
M1 for maximum friction 0.3 × 20 cos 25° = 5.44 N
A1 for 8.45 > 5.44, so the particle slides

parts.examinerComment: Candidates needed to compare the two forces explicitly and state a conclusion.

parts.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line with constant acceleration {a} m s⁻². Its initial velocity is {u} m s⁻¹. Find its displacement after {t} s, in m.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A stone is dropped from rest from a height of {h} m above the ground. Find the time it takes to reach the ground, in seconds, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A particle moves in a straight line so that its velocity t seconds after leaving O is v = {a}t − t² m s⁻¹. Find the greatest velocity of the particle, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who used calculus recognised that the greatest velocity occurs when the acceleration is zero.

parts.prompt: A train starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to {v} m s⁻¹ in {t1} s. It travels at this speed for T s and then decelerates uniformly to rest in {t3} s. The total distance travelled is {=v*(t1/2 + T + t3/2)} m. Find T.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using the area under a velocity-time graph
M1 for equating to {=v*(t1/2 + T + t3/2)}

parts.examinerComment: A sketch of the velocity-time graph helped candidates to structure their working.

parts.prompt: A ball is projected vertically upwards at {u} m s⁻¹ from the top of a cliff {h} m above the sea. Find the time taken for the ball to reach the sea, in seconds, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Choosing upwards as positive and giving the displacement as −{h} m was the cleanest method.

parts.prompt: A particle A of mass {m1} kg moving at {u} m s⁻¹ collides directly with a particle B of mass {m2} kg which is at rest. After the collision B moves at {=u+s} m s⁻¹. Find the speed of A after the collision, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Particles P and Q, of masses {m1} kg and {m2} kg, move towards each other along a straight line with speeds {u1} m s⁻¹ and {u2} m s⁻¹. They collide and coalesce. Find the speed of the combined particle, in m s⁻¹.

markingPoints.text: M1 for momentum with a negative sign for Q: {m1} × {u1} − {m2} × {u2}

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who drew a before-and-after diagram with a positive direction rarely made sign errors.

parts.prompt: Particle A, of mass {a} kg, moving at {u} m s⁻¹, collides with particle B, of mass {=a+dd} kg, which is at rest. After the collision A is at rest. B then collides with and coalesces with particle C, of mass {c} kg, which is at rest. Find the speed of the combined particle, in m s⁻¹.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates who noticed that the total momentum {=a*u} kg m s⁻¹ is unchanged throughout could go straight to the answer.

questions.stem: Particles A and B, of masses 4 kg and m kg, move towards each other along a straight line with speeds 3 m s⁻¹ and 2 m s⁻¹ respectively. After they collide, both move in A's original direction, A with speed 0.5 m s⁻¹ and B with speed 2 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find m.

markingPoints.text: M1 for conservation of momentum with correct signs

parts.examinerComment: Taking A's original direction as positive, B's initial velocity is −2 m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the loss of kinetic energy in the collision.

markingPoints.text: M1 for KE before: ½ × 4 × 3² + ½ × 2.5 × 2² = 23 J
M1 for KE after: ½ × 4 × 0.5² + ½ × 2.5 × 2² = 5.5 J

parts.examinerComment: Kinetic energy is not conserved in this collision. Some candidates used velocity rather than speed squared with a sign.

parts.prompt: A box of mass {m} kg is pulled up a rough plane inclined at {th}° to the horizontal by a force of {=m*k} N acting parallel to the plane. The coefficient of friction is {mu}. Find the acceleration of the box, in m s⁻², correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Friction acts down the plane because the box moves up it. Omitting the weight component was a common error.

parts.prompt: A car of mass {M} kg tows a trailer of mass {m} kg along a straight horizontal road using a light rigid tow-bar. The driving force is {D} N. The resistances to motion are {R1} N on the car and {R2} N on the trailer. Find the tension in the tow-bar, in N, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: A1 for a = {=(D - R1 - R2)/(M + m)}
A1 for T = {=m*(D - R1 - R2)/(M + m) + R2}

parts.examinerComment: Considering the trailer alone is easier than the car alone as fewer forces act on it.

parts.prompt: A particle A of mass {m1} kg rests on a smooth horizontal table. It is attached to a light inextensible string which passes over a smooth pulley at the edge of the table to a particle B of mass {m2} kg hanging freely. The system is released from rest. Find the tension in the string, in N, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for an equation for B: {=10*m2} − T = {m2}a
M1 for an equation for A: T = {m1}a

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates assumed the tension equals the weight of B, which is only true in equilibrium.

parts.prompt: A woman of mass {m} kg stands in a lift which is moving upwards and decelerating at {a} m s⁻². Find the magnitude of the normal reaction between the woman and the floor of the lift, in N.

markingPoints.text: M1 for an equation of motion with acceleration downwards

parts.examinerComment: Moving upwards while decelerating means the acceleration is downwards. Many candidates added instead of subtracting.

parts.prompt: A particle is released from rest on a rough plane inclined at {th}° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is {mu}. Find the time taken for the particle to slide {d} m down the plane, in seconds, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for mg sin {th}° − {mu}mg cos {th}° = ma

parts.examinerComment: The mass cancels. Candidates who kept m in their equations usually still succeeded.

parts.prompt: A car of mass {m} kg moves along a straight level road. The engine works at {P} kW and the resistance to motion is {R} N. Find the acceleration of the car at the instant when its speed is {v} m s⁻¹, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Converting kilowatts to watts was essential.

parts.prompt: A car of mass {m} kg travels up a straight hill inclined at an angle α to the horizontal, where sin α = 1/{k}. The engine works at {P} kW and the resistance to motion is {R} N. Find the greatest possible speed of the car up the hill, in m s⁻¹, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for at greatest speed, driving force = {R} + {m}g sin α

parts.examinerComment: At the greatest speed the acceleration is zero. Many candidates omitted the weight component.

parts.prompt: A particle is projected with speed {u} m s⁻¹ up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane inclined at {th}° to the horizontal. The coefficient of friction is {mu}. Use an energy method to find the distance the particle travels up the plane before coming to rest, in m, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for PE gain = mg d sin {th}°
M1 for ½m{u}² = mgd sin {th}° + {mu}mg cos {th}° × d

parts.examinerComment: The work done against friction must be included alongside the gain in potential energy.

parts.prompt: A child of mass {m} kg slides from rest down a slide. The top of the slide is {h} m vertically above the bottom. The child reaches the bottom with speed {v} m s⁻¹. Find the work done against resistance, in J.

markingPoints.text: M1 for WD = PE loss − KE gain

parts.examinerComment: Well answered. The length of the slide is not needed.

parts.prompt: A pump raises {M} kg of water per minute through a vertical height of {H} m and ejects it with speed {v} m s⁻¹. Find the power of the pump, in W, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for mass per second = {=M/60} kg
M1 for KE per second = ½ × {=M/60} × {v}²

parts.examinerComment: Power is work done per second, so the mass must be converted to a rate per second.

parts.prompt: Group A has {n1} students with a mean mark of {m1}. Group B has {n2} students with a mean mark of {m2}. Find the mean mark of all the students combined, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Averaging the two means, ({m1} + {m2})/2, ignores the different group sizes.

parts.prompt: For a set of {n} values of x, Σ(x − 50) = {A} and Σ(x − 50)² = {B}. Find the standard deviation of x, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Coding does not change the standard deviation, so no adjustment for the 50 is needed. Some candidates subtracted 50 again.

parts.prompt: State one advantage and one disadvantage of using a box-and-whisker plot rather than a histogram to represent a large set of continuous data.

markingPoints.text: B1 for an advantage, e.g. shows the median and quartiles directly; easy to compare two data sets; shows the spread and skewness clearly
B1 for a disadvantage, e.g. does not show the frequencies or detailed shape of the distribution; does not show the mode

parts.examinerComment: Answers needed to refer to specific features of the diagrams. Vague comments such as 'easier to read' gained no credit.

parts.prompt: In a histogram, the class 20 ≤ x < 30, which has frequency {f1}, is represented by a bar of height {=k*f1/10} cm. The class 30 ≤ x < {=30+w} has frequency {f2}. Find the height of its bar, in cm.

markingPoints.text: M1 for frequency density of first class = {=f1/10}
M1 for scale: {k} cm per unit of frequency density

parts.examinerComment: Bar heights are proportional to frequency density, not frequency.

parts.prompt: The marks of two classes in the same test are summarised. Class P: median 54, interquartile range 12. Class Q: median 61, interquartile range 25. Make two comparisons between the marks of the two classes.

markingPoints.text: B1 for Class Q had higher marks on average (higher median)
B1 for Class Q's marks were more spread out / less consistent (larger IQR)

parts.examinerComment: Comparisons must be made in context and refer to both average and spread.

parts.prompt: {a} identical red counters and {b} identical blue counters are arranged in a row. Find the number of different arrangements.
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: A team of {r} people is to be chosen from {n} people, including Asha. In how many ways can the team be chosen if Asha must be included?
parts.examinerComment: Once Asha is chosen, {=r-1} more are chosen from the remaining {=n-1}.

parts.prompt: Find the number of ways in which {n} people can sit in a row if two particular people must not sit next to each other.
parts.examinerComment: Subtracting from the total is the most efficient method.

parts.prompt: A committee of {r} people is to be chosen from {m} men and {w} women. Find the number of different committees that include at least one woman.

markingPoints.text: M1 for subtracting C({m}, {r}) with no women

parts.examinerComment: Candidates who listed the cases (1 woman, 2 women, …) often missed a case.

parts.prompt: Find the number of different arrangements of the letters of the word PARALLEL in which the three L's are together.

markingPoints.text: M1 for treating LLL as a single unit, giving 6 units
M1 for dividing by 2! for the repeated A

parts.examinerComment: Forgetting the repeated A, giving 720, was the most common error.

parts.prompt: A bag contains {r} red and {b} blue discs. Two discs are taken at random without replacement. Find the probability that they are the same colour, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for adding the blue case

parts.examinerComment: Without replacement, the second probability has a denominator one less.

parts.prompt: On any day, the probability that Sam takes the bus is {p}. If he takes the bus, the probability that he is late is {q1}; otherwise the probability that he is late is {q2}. Given that Sam is late, find the probability that he took the bus, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: A tree diagram helped candidates identify the two branches that lead to being late.

parts.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown. Find the probability that the sum of the scores is {s}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for counting {=6 - abs(s - 7)} outcomes from 36

parts.examinerComment: A sample-space diagram makes counting reliable.

parts.prompt: Events A and B are independent with P(A) = {a} and P(B) = {b}. Find the probability that exactly one of A and B occurs.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found P(A ∪ B) instead, which includes both events occurring.

parts.prompt: Events A and B are such that P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.7. Determine, with a reason, whether A and B are independent.

markingPoints.text: A1 for P(A) × P(B) = 0.15 ≠ 0.1, so not independent

parts.examinerComment: A numerical comparison is required. Statements such as 'they can happen together' do not show independence.

parts.prompt: X ~ B({n}, {p}). Find P(X ≥ 1), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Using 1 − P(X = 0) is much quicker than adding the other probabilities.

parts.prompt: X ~ B({n}, {p}). Find Var(X).
parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: The random variable X has a geometric distribution with probability of success {p} on each trial. Find P(X > {r}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: X > {r} means the first {r} trials are all failures.

parts.prompt: The random variable X takes the values 1, 2, …, {n}, and P(X = x) = kx. Find E(X), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Finding k first was essential.

parts.prompt: Two fair six-sided dice are thrown and X is the larger of the two scores (or the common score if they are equal). Draw up the probability distribution of X.

markingPoints.text: M1 for using a sample-space diagram or counting
A1 for at least three probabilities correct

parts.examinerComment: Checking that the probabilities sum to 1 would have helped many candidates.

parts.prompt: X ~ N({mu}, {=s^2}). Find P({=mu-d1} < X < {=mu+d2}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: A sketch helped candidates to combine the two areas correctly.

parts.prompt: X ~ N({mu}, σ²). Given that P(X > {=mu+d}) = 0.1, find σ, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should use the critical values table for 10%, which gives 1.282.

parts.prompt: The lengths of rods are normally distributed with mean {mu} cm and standard deviation {s} cm. In a batch of {n} rods, find the expected number with length greater than {=mu+d} cm, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The expected number need not be a whole number.

parts.prompt: The random variable X is normally distributed. P(X < 30) = 0.2 and P(X > 50) = 0.1. Find the mean and standard deviation of X.
parts.examinerComment: Sign errors in the first equation were common: 30 is below the mean, so its z-value is negative.

parts.prompt: X ~ B({n}, {p}). Use a suitable normal approximation to find P(X ≤ {=n*p-c}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Candidates should check np > 5 and n(1 − p) > 5 before using the approximation.

parts.prompt: X ~ Po({l}). Find P(X ≥ 2), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates found 1 − P(X ≤ 2) instead.

parts.prompt: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions Po({a}) and Po({b}). Find P(X + Y = {r}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Using the sum of the independent Poisson variables is much quicker than listing combinations.

parts.prompt: X ~ B({n}, {p}). Use a suitable Poisson approximation to find P(X = {r}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The approximation is valid because n is large and np is small.

parts.prompt: A call centre receives calls at an average rate of 3 per minute. State two assumptions needed for the number of calls received in one minute to be modelled by a Poisson distribution.

markingPoints.text: B1 for calls arrive independently of each other
B1 for calls arrive at a constant average rate / singly / at random

parts.examinerComment: Assumptions should be given in context. 'Events are independent' without reference to calls gained less credit.
