parts.prompt: X ~ Po({l}). Use a suitable normal approximation to find P(X > {=l+c}), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Using {=l+c-0.5} instead of {=l+c+0.5} was a common error: X > {=l+c} means X ≥ {=l+c+1}.

parts.prompt: The masses of bags of flour are normally distributed with mean {mu} kg and standard deviation {s} kg. Find the probability that the total mass of {n} randomly chosen bags exceeds {=n*mu+d} kg, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The variance of a sum of {n} independent values is {n}σ², not {=n^2}σ².

parts.prompt: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N({m1}, {=s1^2}) and N({m2}, {=s2^2}). Find P(X > Y), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Variances add when variables are subtracted.

parts.prompt: The random variable X has variance {v}. Find the standard deviation of {a}X − {b}, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Subtracting a constant does not change the spread. Some candidates multiplied the variance by {a} instead of {=a^2}.

parts.prompt: The independent random variables X and Y have distributions N({m1}, {=s1^2}) and N({m2}, {=s2^2}). Find P(2X − Y > 0), correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: Var(2X) = 4Var(X). Using 2Var(X) was the most common error.

parts.prompt: The random variable X has variance σ². Explain the difference between 2X and X₁ + X₂, where X₁ and X₂ are independent observations of X, and state the variance of each.

markingPoints.text: B1 for 2X is one observation doubled; X₁ + X₂ is the sum of two separate observations

parts.examinerComment: Many candidates gave the variances correctly but could not explain the distinction.

parts.prompt: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = k({a} − x) for 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}, and 0 otherwise. Find the median of X, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ from 0 to m of k({a} − x) dx = 0.5
A1 for a correct quadratic in m

parts.examinerComment: The root greater than {a} must be rejected because it lies outside the range of X.

parts.prompt: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = 3x²/{=a^3} for 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}, and 0 otherwise. Find Var(X), correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for E(X) = ∫ x f(x) dx = {=3*a/4}
M1 for E(X²) = ∫ x² f(x) dx = {=3*a^2/5}

parts.examinerComment: Forgetting to subtract the square of the mean was a common error.

parts.prompt: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = k/x² for 1 ≤ x ≤ {b}, and 0 otherwise. Find the value of k.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ from 1 to {b} of k/x² dx = 1

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: The continuous random variable X has probability density function f(x) = 2x/{=a^2} for 0 ≤ x ≤ {a}, and 0 otherwise. Find P(X > {b}), correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: M1 for ∫ from {b} to {a} of 2x/{=a^2} dx

parts.examinerComment: Well answered.

parts.prompt: Explain why the function f(x) = x − 1 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3, and 0 otherwise, cannot be a probability density function.

markingPoints.text: B1 for a probability density function cannot take negative values

parts.examinerComment: Some candidates checked only that the area equals 1. Here the total area is 1.5, which is a second reason.

parts.prompt: The standard deviation of a population is {s}. A random sample of {=k^2} observations has mean {m}. Find the upper limit of a 95% confidence interval for the population mean, correct to 2 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Some candidates used the variance rather than the standard deviation in the formula.

parts.prompt: A population has standard deviation {s}. Find the smallest sample size needed for the width of a 95% confidence interval for the population mean to be less than {w}.
parts.examinerComment: The width of the interval is twice the margin of error. The answer must be rounded up.

parts.prompt: In a random sample of {n} voters, {x} said they would vote for Party A. Find the upper limit of an approximate 90% confidence interval for the proportion of all voters who would vote for Party A, correct to 3 decimal places.
parts.examinerComment: Using 1.96 for a 90% interval was a common error.

parts.prompt: The number of faults per metre in a fabric has distribution Po({l}). A random sample of {n} one-metre lengths is taken. Use a suitable approximation to find the probability that the sample mean exceeds {=l+d}, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for using the Central Limit Theorem

parts.examinerComment: The Central Limit Theorem applies because the sample is large, even though the population is not normal.

parts.prompt: Explain why it was necessary to use the Central Limit Theorem in finding a confidence interval for the mean of a population whose distribution is unknown, and state why it may be used here when the sample size is 80.

markingPoints.text: B1 for the population distribution is not known to be normal
B1 for the sample is large (n = 80), so the sample mean is approximately normally distributed

parts.examinerComment: The Central Limit Theorem concerns the distribution of the sample mean, not of the population.

parts.prompt: A test is carried out to see whether a new fertiliser increases the mean yield of a crop. Explain what is meant by a Type II error in this context.

markingPoints.text: B1 for concluding that the fertiliser does not increase the mean yield
B1 for when in fact it does

parts.examinerComment: Answers must be in context. Many candidates described a Type I error.

parts.prompt: A population has standard deviation {s}. A test is carried out of H₀: μ = {mu} against H₁: μ > {mu}. A random sample of {=k^2} values has mean {=mu+d}. Find the value of the test statistic, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: The standard deviation of the sample mean is σ/√n.

parts.prompt: A machine fills bags with sugar. The masses are normally distributed with mean 500 g and standard deviation 8 g. After servicing, a random sample of 25 bags has mean mass 497 g. Test at the 5% significance level whether the mean mass has decreased.

markingPoints.text: B1 for H₀: μ = 500, H₁: μ < 500
A1 for reject H₀: there is evidence that the mean mass has decreased

parts.examinerComment: Conclusions should not be over-assertive: 'there is evidence that' rather than 'it is proved that'.

parts.prompt: The number of accidents per month on a road has distribution Po({l}). After a new speed limit, there is 1 accident in a month. Find the probability, assuming the rate is unchanged, of 1 or fewer accidents in a month, correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.examinerComment: This is the p-value for a test of whether the rate has decreased.

parts.prompt: A test of H₀: p = {p} against H₁: p < {p} uses 10 trials. H₀ is rejected if X ≤ 1. Find the probability of a Type I error, correct to 3 significant figures.

markingPoints.text: B1 for a Type I error occurs when X ≤ 1 given p = {p}

parts.examinerComment: The probability of a Type I error is the probability of the critical region when H₀ is true.
